why: Both wrap the same single client and verify all five call sites live, but A's inventory is more complete (it finds the VMind Node subprocess posting to <base_url>/chat/completions with the app's provider key, which B omits entirely) and its host unlock covers every shipped config shape rather than only api.anthropic.com. On system judgment the two are close — B has two sharper individual insights (per-agent spend labels, and the measured fact that temperature-bearing requests silently drop *-5 fallback candidates) — but A ships more of its judgment as tested branches, adds the provider_timeout and token-accounting levers B lacks, and B leaves its two best ideas unbuilt and overlapping A's.
A_best: Found and honestly reported the LLM call sites outside the Python process (VMind chart subprocess posting to /chat/completions with the provider key, Browser Use MCP, Azure, Bedrock) and shipped the vision-catalog fix that stops the browser agent's screenshots being silently dropped on every current model — a real behaviour bug Router cannot paper over, measured before/after.
B_best: The fallback item: it caught, by measurement, that the runtime's capability guard silently drops any candidate whose catalog entry rejects temperature, so a naive fallback list on this app (which always sends temperature) would be a no-op — plus per-agent spend labels keyed on the config_name the app already has, a dimension A never exploits.
A_worst: Neither engineer clears the CTO bar — no spend caps, shadow models, Jev or Switchyard, and no per-feature model tiering — and A defers the single largest lever (which model serves ask_tool, and what it falls back to) entirely to a decision item; its blanket host unlock also routes Google/aggregator configs whose catalog ids are BYOK or non-matching, a case B reasoned through and A did not.
B_worst: Missed the VMind subprocess call site completely, so its claim to have covered the app's LLM traffic is incomplete; it also declined provider_timeout on reasoning that gets it backwards (a client-side timeout does not stop Router generating, so the abandoned tokens are billed either way), and three of its five improvements are proposals that largely duplicate what A already built and tested.
